0: <s>Tattvaratnāvalokaḥ</s> (The Illumination of the Jewel of Reality)
1: <s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the feet of the glorious true teacher (<s>Sadguru</s>)!
2: He who is of the form of incomparable bliss, <s>Śrīnivāsa</s> (Abode of Śrī), the shelterless one, who possesses the knowledge in the form of the ten incomparable Goddesses,
3: who brings about the attainment of happiness for the welfare of the three worlds, the changeless one — may <s>Kamalapāṇi</s> (the Lotus-Handed One) be victorious as long as the directions expand! (verse 1)
4: Those who do not know the form of the beautiful fourth empowerment (<s>caturtha-seka</s>) attained through the procedure of the glorious <s>mantra</s>, which is devoid of explicit words —
5: for their clear understanding, an effort is made with the seven divisions combined with groups of various instructions. (verse 2)
6: For all the sectarians (<s>tīrthyas</s>) are confused in knowing the nature of reality (<s>tattva</s>) and of the goal (<s>sādhya</s>).
7: Among them, the knower of <s>tattva</s> is said to be the highest — so goes the popular saying about the <s>Vedāntins</s>. (verse 3)
8: The <s>Vedāntins</s> declare the goal (<s>sādhya</s>) to be of the nature of bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), unshakeable by self-knowledge, peaceful;
9: and the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Khaḍgas), and <s>Jains</s> desire the goal to be the cessation of the material conditions (<s>upadhi</s>) of form and the like. (verse 4)
10: Devoid of form, having the nature of the sky and moon, knowable by one's own self, and full of the essence of compassion,
11: adorned with the marks of existence, purposeful, issuing forth generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the like, devoid of [worldly] happiness — (verse 5)
12: with body adorned by marks of bliss and existence, enjoyed by those abiding on the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>),
13: those who follow the method of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) beginning with generosity declare the goal to be one that works for the benefit of beings. (verse 6)
14: Having fulfilled all qualities such as generosity, having fully awakened, and having accomplished all that is to be done,
15: that which is the direct cause of the limit of existence (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) — that goal too is of the nature of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). (verse 7)
16: Embracing one's own consort, working for that purpose, of the nature of liberation from both suffering and happiness,
17: they declare the goal to be with body adorned by eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), beyond conceptual elaboration (<s>kalpanā</s>). (verse 8)
18: Devoid of the particular form of one's own deity, having previously established bliss as clear and real,
19: someone has declared [the goal] to be called <s>mahāsukha</s> (great bliss), working for the benefit of the world, resembling a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>). (verse 9)
20: Having directly accomplished one's own lord (<s>svādhipa</s>) in the form of bliss,
21: afterward, having abandoned [that form], bliss alone would be the fruit. The pure [reality] cannot be directly accomplished; therefore the form of one's own lord is meditated upon. (verse 10)
22: With a body like space, with limbs adorned by marks, full of incomparable bliss, united with one's own consort (<s>svābhā</s>),
23: a certain radiant, immeasurable lord of sages, working for the benefit of all beings, declares the goal to be free from annihilation (<s>uccheda</s>). (verse 11)
24: Having directly accomplished one's own lord in the form of bliss, the fruit would be mere knowledge of meditative equanimity (<s>bhāvopekṣā</s>).
25: Lasting as long as <s>saṃsāra</s>, working for the benefit of beings, resembling a wish-fulfilling jewel, absolutely peaceful. (verse 12)
26: Having directly accomplished the <s>maṇḍala</s> in the form of bliss, and afterward its dissolution by one's own will —
27: is there or is there not an absence of benefiting beings in this? Because there is manifestation [again] from dissolution. (verse 13)
28: Having clearly created the desired form of these [practitioners], someone says the fruit afterward is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>).
29: And since cessation is of non-different form, therefore even in the difference of position there is no [real] difference. (verse 14)
30: After the knowledge of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the tasting of <s>bodhicitta</s> — the fourth [empowerment] — [some say] the remaining empowerment is the highest,
31: since all effort in meditations (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is futile, because the attainment of its fruit is already well-established. (verse 15)
32: After the knowledge of <s>prajñā</s>, the tasting of the delight attained — the fourth empowerment is called the lowest [by others],
33: since all effort in meditation and the like taught by the <s>Buddha</s> would [then] be attached and fruitless. (verse 16)
34: The <s>vajra</s>-seed, purified and cleansed by hearing (<s>śruti</s>), becoming a pure lotus-sprout, growing to nourishment —
35: the fourth crop (<s>turīya-śasya</s>) reaches full ripeness: the fourth [empowerment] is clear, yet hidden even from the wise. (verse 17)
36: The five lamps, drops of nectar, the moon, the <s>maṇḍalas</s> arising from the drop between the eyebrows,
37: the nature of the wind (<s>vāyu</s>), the uvula (<s>galaśuṇḍikā</s>) and so forth — these are not the true nature; one should investigate for oneself. (verse 18)
38: By [similes of] dream, magic (<s>indrajāla</s>), reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>), illusion (<s>māyā</s>), mirage (<s>marīci</s>), <s>gandharva</s>-city, and moon in water,
39: and by all other designated similes — the goal (<s>sādhya</s>) is nothing other than what has been stated here. (verse 19)
40: By words such as 'profound' (<s>gambhīra</s>), 'empty' (<s>śūnya</s>), 'mere appearance' (<s>pratibhāsamātra</s>), 'peaceful' (<s>śānta</s>), 'extremely subtle' (<s>atisūkṣma</s>), 'inexpressible' (<s>anabhilāpya</s>),
41: 'unstained' (<s>nirlepa</s>), 'formless' (<s>nīrūpa</s>), 'untainted' (<s>nirañjana</s>), and the like — confusion should not be created regarding the reality of the other goal. (verse 20)
43: This is the composition of the venerable Paṇḍita <s>Vāgīśvarakīrti</s>.
